title: The Animal Apocalypse
lead: A Jewish vision in 1 Enoch 85–90, which most scholars date to about 164–160 BC, that retells the history of the world from Adam to the end with animals standing for people: Israel as sheep, the nations as wild beasts and birds, angels as men, fallen angels as stars, and God as "the Lord of the sheep." The Ethiopian Orthodox churches read it as Scripture, as part of 1 Enoch; other churches read it as an ancient Jewish writing.

sections.b: The Bible often pictures peoples as animals: Israel as God's flock (Psalm 80:1; Ezekiel 34), empires as beasts (Daniel 7–8), a king as a ram (Daniel 8:3–4). The Animal Apocalypse turns that habit into a whole history. Bulls stand for the righteous line from Adam to Isaac, sheep for Israel from Jacob on, unclean animals and birds of prey for the nations, and seventy angelic "shepherds" for the powers that rule Israel from the exile to the Maccabean revolt. It ends with a judgment, a new house, and all peoples changed into white cattle.
